reviewed_properties.assessment: asyncio.wait(FIRST_COMPLETED) observes the original sender without cancelling it. sender.result() runs before accepting the marker whenever the sender is already done, preserving its exact exception or CancelledError even when the marker is also ready. A successful completed sender without a marker asserts instead of hanging or accepting missing evidence. All three changed PG marker sites pass the actual newly created control_task Task.

The helper owns only Event.wait's task and cancels/joins it in finally; cancelling the observer does not cancel the sender through asyncio.wait. SOURCE and PG callers retain their original task ownership, release pause events, cancel only pending owned tasks and gather them. PG registers each sender/second/stopper before its next await. PG observes the first error before cleanup and re-raises it; return_exceptions=True is cleanup, not the success oracle. No newly introduced orphan, unbounded await of an unbounded producer, or primary-error suppression was identified in this delta.

Changed joins directly await the already-created public control_task; none creates a fresh task, shield, retry or replacement four-second timeout. control_task retains asyncio.timeout(4), including its original writer close/finally with wait_closed bounded by 0.2 seconds. NativeTaskOwner retains its original absolute four-second owner deadline, and LocalControl retains its own four-second handling deadline. Product bytes are unchanged.

reviewed_properties.assessment: The six real control_task/LocalControl UDS cases cover a 2.1-second marker, original deadline before/after a marker, early exact conflict, sender cancellation and success without a marker. Timeout negatives require the sender done, not cancelled, with exact TimeoutError and elapsed 4 <= t < 4.25. An outer 4.25-second rescue timeout therefore cannot satisfy PASS by cancelling a still-pending sender. Separate controls cover simultaneous failure, observer-only waiter ownership and actual duplicate/conflict SOURCE callers with a delayed 2.1-second first reply. Final task and socket/client assertions support owned cleanup at the stated SOURCE boundary.
